fixes.title: It ruled out the true cause because of a change description
fixes.problem: Asked only what the incident cost (B3), the copilot got both numbers right, then volunteered a cause: it dismissed the decline-code map release because the change log said the release only added code R65. That release had also turned R05 into a hard decline. The judge failed the answer.
fixes.change: Two rules added to the instructions. A change's description may not list all its effects, so check its footprint in the data before ruling it out. And name only causes you have checked: if the question asks for numbers, answer the numbers and say which checks you did not run. In run 2 the copilot answered the cost and listed the checks it had not run.

fixes.title: It sized the calendar day instead of the incident
fixes.problem: Asked why approval dropped on 13 August (B1), the copilot found both causes but sized the whole day: −7.1 points and 82 approvals. The incident ran from 14:00 to 12:10 the next day and cost 110 approvals. The judge passed the answer and flagged the understatement; I count it as a failure.
fixes.change: New first step in the method: find the window with the hourly data and the change log, size that window and say which one was used. In run 2 the copilot sized 13 Aug 14:00 to 14 Aug 12:10.

fixes.title: It claimed something was absent beyond what it had checked
fixes.problem: Run 3 found a new failure mode. Asked whether there was an early warning (C3), the copilot found the retry alert from 6 August and sized the incident correctly, but its change-log query stopped at 15 August 00:00 and it wrote that the log showed no mapping change through 15 August. The hotfix was logged at 08:00 that day, so its first recommendation rested on a false premise. The judge failed the answer.
fixes.change: New rule, added before run 4: when the copilot says something did not happen (no change, no alert, no notice), it gives the period it checked and does not extend the claim beyond it. In runs 4 and 5 C3 passed, and each such statement came with its period, for example "change log for CO, 1 Jun to 15 Aug 00:00".

showcase.question: Why did the approval rate for debit cards in Colombia drop on 13 August 2026?
showcase.answer:
**Short answer**
At 14:00 on 13 Aug (Bogota time) routing v14 (CHG-0813, described as cost optimization, -40 bps) sent 100% of Colombian domestic debit to Acquirer B. B approved far less of this traffic than Acquirer A had, and it does not retry its most common decline, '05 Do not honor', because the decline-code map v2.3 (CHG-0806, live since 6 Aug) classifies that code as hard on B. The drop ended when v14 was rolled back to v13 at 12:10 on 14 Aug (CHG-0814, incident INC-0814). I sized and explained that window (13 Aug 14:00 to 14 Aug 12:10), not the calendar day. The primary cause is acquirer-side (routing to B). The 05 classification is a contributing factor that stopped the cascade from softening the loss.

**Impact** (Colombia, debit, domestic, final approval rate; baseline = the 14 days before the window start, all first-routed to Acquirer A on v13)
- Incident window: 75.6% vs 86.5% baseline, -10.95 pp, on 1,004 payments (first-attempt rate 70.7% vs 84.6%). 759 approvals vs 869 expected: 110 lost approvals and USD 6,354 of lost approved volume (USD 47,096 approved of USD 61,689 attempted).
- Calendar day 13 Aug: 79.4% (913 approved of 1,150 sent) vs 86.7% 28-day baseline, -7.33 pp, flagged as an anomaly. The first 14 hours were normal (85.9% vs 86.5% baseline, 3 approvals below expected) and the last 10 hours ran on B. 14 Aug closed at 84.6% because the rollback came at 12:10.
- After the rollback (14 Aug 12:10 to 24:00): 850 payments, all on A / v13, 87.4% (12 Aug: 87.2%; 15 Aug: 85.3%).

**Evidence**
- Window: the change log for CO between 3 Aug 00:00 and 15 Aug 00:00 (Bogota time) holds only CHG-0806 (6 Aug), CHG-0813 (13 Aug 14:00) and the rollback CHG-0814 (14 Aug 12:10). Hourly data agree: A had all first-routed payments until 13:59 (hourly final rate 83.0% to 88.6% from 07:00); from 14:00 B had all of them and the hourly rate ran between 58.0% (22:00) and 83.1% (16:00).
- Who moved (fn_approval_drivers): B / routing v14 had 100% of payments in the window (0% in the baseline: B had no CO debit payments in the previous 14 days) and explains -10.95 pp, the entire change. All eight issuers (CO-ISS-01 to CO-ISS-08), both card brands, 3DS-authenticated and not, and every merchant segment with volume fell too, so this is not an issuer-side event. Each dimension sums to the same -10.95 pp, so do not add across dimensions.

**Declines and retries in the window** (B has no CO debit baseline, so it is compared with A's baseline)

| Code | B, window: % of payments (failures) | A, baseline: % of payments (failures) | Retried on a 2nd acquirer, B vs A | Map class, B vs A |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 05 Do not honor | 13.7% (137) | 4.1% (628) | 0.0% vs 98.4% | hard vs soft |
| 1A 3DS required | 5.2% (52) | 1.1% (167) | 100.0% vs 99.4% | soft vs soft |
| 51 Insufficient funds | 3.8% (38) | 4.2% (638) | 0.0% vs 0.0% | soft vs soft |
| 91 Issuer or switch unavailable | 1.2% (12) | 0.5% (72) | 100.0% vs 98.6% | soft vs soft |

Every other code on B was 1.0% of payments or less. On A in the baseline the cascade recovered 21.7% of the 05 declines; on B none were retried. B's other retryable codes (1A, 91, 96, technical errors, timeouts) were retried at 100%, so the cascade worked wherever the map allowed it. Code 51 is not retried on either acquirer, so it is not a change.

**Was CHG-0806 involved? Yes, through an effect its description does not list.** The description only says 'adds R65 handling'. In gold_cascade_daily (1 Jun to 12 Aug, B's first attempts in CO and MX, credit and debit combined, cross-border included), B's code 05 went from soft and retryable under v2.2 (1 Jun to 6 Aug: 3,296 failures, all retried, 1,237 recovered) to hard and not retryable under v2.3 (6 to 12 Aug: 331 failures, 0 retried). On A and C, 05 stayed soft and retryable under v2.3. No other B code changed class (code 65 appears only under v2.3). Because B had no CO debit traffic before, the effect only reached CO debit when v14 put all of it on B.

**Recommended action**
1. Keep Colombian debit on A / v13. If the cost saving is still wanted, bring B in as a gradual canary (a small share of CO debit) with an hourly approval guardrail against A and an automatic rollback. v14 went from 0% to 100% in one step and ran for about 22 hours before the rollback.
2. Ask the owner of the decline-code map whether B's code 05 was meant to become hard in v2.3 (it is soft and retryable on A and C, and was on B under v2.2). If not, restore it. This also affects B's traffic in other segments since 6 Aug (331 B declines on 05 in CO and MX through 12 Aug, none retried); I did not size the approvals lost there.
3. Ask Acquirer B why '05 Do not honor' and '1A 3DS required' were so much more frequent than on A for the same issuers (13.7% and 5.2% of payments vs 4.1% and 1.1%). The data cannot explain it.
4. Re-check the cost case before any retry: the saving is described as -40 bps on approved volume (USD 47,096 in the window), while the lost approved volume was USD 6,354. I did not verify the saving in the fee data (fees paid in the window: USD 1,186.03).

**What I could not establish or did not check**
- How much of the -10.95 pp comes from B's higher decline rates versus the missing 05 retry. For scale: if the 137 declines on 05 had been retried at A's CO debit baseline recovery rate (21.7%), the cascade would have won back only part of the 110 lost approvals, so fixing the mapping alone would not bring B to A's level.
- The fee saving of v14 (fees on A vs B), and the impact of the 05 reclassification outside CO debit.
- Why B returns more 05 and 1A declines: acquirer configuration is not in the data.
- Scope: domestic traffic only, Bogota local time. Window figures use the 14-day baseline before the window start; the daily figures use the 28-day trailing baseline.
queries: SELECT hour_local_ts, sum(payments_sent) AS sent, round(sum(first_attempt_approved) / NULLIF(sum(payments_sent), 0), 4) AS first_rate, round(sum(final_approved) / NULLIF(sum(payments_sent), 0), 4) AS final_rate, sum(CASE WHEN acquirer_id = 'A' THEN payments_sent ELSE 0 END) AS a_sent, round(sum(CASE WHEN acquirer_id = 'A' THEN final_approved ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(sum(CASE WHEN acquirer_id = 'A' THEN payments_sent ELSE 0 END), 0), 4) AS a_final_rate, sum(CASE WHEN acquirer_id = 'B' THEN payments_sent ELSE 0 END) AS b_sent, round(sum(CASE WHEN acquirer_id = 'B' THEN final_approved ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(sum(CASE WHEN acquirer_id = 'B' THEN payments_sent ELSE 0 END), 0), 4) AS b_final_rate, sum(CASE WHEN acquirer_id = 'C' THEN payments_sent ELSE 0 END) AS c_sent, round(sum(CASE WHEN acquirer_id = 'C' THEN final_approved ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(sum(CASE WHEN acquirer_id = 'C' THEN payments_sent ELSE 0 END), 0), 4) AS c_final_rate FROM workspace.approval_copilot.gold_approval_hourly WHERE country = 'CO' AND card_type = 'debit' AND NOT is_cross_border AND business_date BETWEEN DATE'2026-08-12' AND DATE'2026-08-14' GROUP BY hour_local_ts ORDER BY hour_local_ts

SELECT business_date, payments_sent, final_approved, round(final_approval_rate, 4) AS final_rate, round(baseline_rate, 4) AS baseline_rate, round(delta_pp, 2) AS delta_pp, round(z_history, 2) AS z_history, round(z_binomial, 2) AS z_binomial, is_anomaly FROM workspace.approval_copilot.gold_anomalies_daily WHERE country = 'CO' AND card_type = 'debit' AND business_date BETWEEN DATE'2026-08-06' AND DATE'2026-08-20' ORDER BY business_date
SELECT * FROM workspace.approval_copilot.fn_changes_near('CO', TIMESTAMP'2026-08-13 00:00:00', TIMESTAMP'2026-08-15 00:00:00', 240) ORDER BY changed_at_utc
SELECT * FROM workspace.approval_copilot.fn_approval_drivers('CO', TIMESTAMP'2026-08-13 00:00:00', TIMESTAMP'2026-08-14 00:00:00', 'debit') ORDER BY abs(total_effect_pp) DESC LIMIT 15
SELECT * FROM workspace.approval_copilot.fn_decline_shift('CO', TIMESTAMP'2026-08-13 00:00:00', TIMESTAMP'2026-08-14 00:00:00', 'debit') ORDER BY delta_pp DESC LIMIT 15

SELECT * FROM workspace.approval_copilot.fn_cascade_health('CO', TIMESTAMP'2026-08-13 00:00:00', TIMESTAMP'2026-08-14 00:00:00', 'debit') WHERE window_failures > 0 ORDER BY acquirer_id, reason_code LIMIT 60

SELECT 'A_before_change_13Aug_00:00_to_14:00' AS period, * FROM workspace.approval_copilot.fn_drop_impact('CO', TIMESTAMP'2026-08-13 00:00:00', TIMESTAMP'2026-08-13 14:00:00', 'debit') UNION ALL SELECT 'B_incident_window_13Aug_14:00_to_14Aug_12:10' AS period, * FROM workspace.approval_copilot.fn_drop_impact('CO', TIMESTAMP'2026-08-13 14:00:00', TIMESTAMP'2026-08-14 12:10:00', 'debit') UNION ALL SELECT 'C_after_rollback_14Aug_12:10_to_15Aug_00:00' AS period, * FROM workspace.approval_copilot.fn_drop_impact('CO', TIMESTAMP'2026-08-14 12:10:00', TIMESTAMP'2026-08-15 00:00:00', 'debit') ORDER BY period

SELECT * FROM (SELECT 'incident_window' AS period, * FROM workspace.approval_copilot.fn_approval_drivers('CO', TIMESTAMP'2026-08-13 14:00:00', TIMESTAMP'2026-08-14 12:10:00', 'debit') UNION ALL SELECT 'after_rollback' AS period, * FROM workspace.approval_copilot.fn_approval_drivers('CO', TIMESTAMP'2026-08-14 12:10:00', TIMESTAMP'2026-08-15 00:00:00', 'debit') WHERE dimension IN ('acquirer', 'routing_rule_version')) AS t ORDER BY period, abs(total_effect_pp) DESC LIMIT 45

WITH d AS (SELECT * FROM workspace.approval_copilot.fn_decline_shift('CO', TIMESTAMP'2026-08-13 14:00:00', TIMESTAMP'2026-08-14 12:10:00', 'debit')), c AS (SELECT * FROM workspace.approval_copilot.fn_cascade_health('CO', TIMESTAMP'2026-08-13 14:00:00', TIMESTAMP'2026-08-14 12:10:00', 'debit')) SELECT coalesce(d.acquirer_id, c.acquirer_id) AS acq, coalesce(d.reason_code, c.reason_code) AS code, d.reason AS reason, d.baseline_failures AS base_fail, d.window_failures AS win_fail, round(d.baseline_pct_of_payments, 2) AS base_pct, round(d.window_pct_of_payments, 2) AS win_pct, round(d.delta_pp, 2) AS delta_pp, c.baseline_cascade_rate AS base_cascade, c.window_cascade_rate AS win_cascade, c.baseline_recovery_rate AS base_recovery, c.window_recovery_rate AS win_recovery, c.baseline_mapped_as AS base_mapped, c.window_mapped_as AS win_mapped, c.window_mapping_versions AS win_versions FROM d FULL OUTER JOIN c ON d.acquirer_id = c.acquirer_id AND d.reason_code = c.reason_code ORDER BY coalesce(d.window_failures, c.window_failures, 0) DESC, acq, code

SELECT acquirer_id, first_reason_code AS reason_code, first_mapping_version AS mapping_version, first_decline_type AS mapped_as, first_retryable AS retryable, sum(first_attempt_failures) AS failures, sum(cascaded) AS cascaded, round(sum(cascaded) / NULLIF(sum(first_attempt_failures), 0), 4) AS cascade_rate, sum(recovered) AS recovered, min(business_date) AS first_day, max(business_date) AS last_day, min(country) AS country_min, max(country) AS country_max, min(card_type) AS card_min, max(card_type) AS card_max FROM workspace.approval_copilot.gold_cascade_daily WHERE business_date < DATE'2026-08-13' AND first_decline_type <> 'none' AND (acquirer_id = 'B' OR first_reason_code = '05') GROUP BY acquirer_id, first_reason_code, first_mapping_version, first_decline_type, first_retryable ORDER BY acquirer_id, first_reason_code, first_mapping_version
showcase.run_label: run 6: Claude Sonnet with the Genie agent's instructions, tables and functions

findings.title: It sized the calendar day again
findings.problem: Asked why Colombian debit dropped on 13 August (B1), Genie found both causes and saw that the drop began at 14:00, then sized 13 August as a whole day: −7.3 points and 84 approvals instead of −10.9 and 110. In chat mode it sized B3 on whole days too. The instruction that fixed this in run 2 did not hold in Genie.
findings.next: Next: example SQL that finds an incident window in the hourly data and sizes it, on dates outside the benchmark, so the pattern sits in the agent's examples as well as in its text.

findings.title: It claimed more than it had checked
findings.problem: Asked about an early warning (C3), Genie queried the retry alerts from 8 August and wrote that they started then, five days before the incident. They started on 6 August. This is the failure mode of run 3, and the rule added after it did not hold either.
findings.next: Next: example SQL that looks for the first alert from the start of the data, and the rule repeated in the description of the alert table.

findings.title: It used the wrong table or metric
findings.problem: It averaged daily p95 latencies into a monthly figure (A4), and ranked issuers by joining hourly rows to a daily table, which measured whole days and put a foreign issuer first in a question about domestic cards (C4).
findings.next: Next: a column description that says daily p95 values cannot be averaged, and example SQL that ranks issuers inside a window with fn_approval_drivers.

findings.title: It explained a recovery it had not checked
findings.problem: It found the risk rule behind the Brazilian conversion drop (B6), but called the recovery “self-corrected”. A logged change, risk rules v3.1 on 20 June, had tuned the rule.
findings.next: Next: a method step that checks the change log until the metric recovers, not only around the start of the drop.

genie.table_note: Genie: the deployed agent, 29 October 2026. A1–A6, B3, C1, C2 and C4 ran in chat mode and were graded by Genie's own benchmark grader, which compares result sets (A5, which it sent to manual review, was graded by hand). The other ten ran in agent mode and were graded by the same judge as the offline runs. C1 failed on the shape of its result: the right winner and gap, in one row instead of one row per acquirer.
